items.stem: What is the key architectural difference between a container and a virtual machine?

options.text: A container shares the host kernel, while a VM runs its own full operating system
options.rationale: Correct: containers share the kernel; VMs virtualise the whole machine.

options.text: A container includes a full separate operating system kernel
options.rationale: That describes a VM, not a container.

options.text: A VM shares the host kernel with other VMs
options.rationale: VMs run their own OS, not a shared kernel.

options.text: There is no difference between them
options.rationale: They differ significantly in isolation and overhead.

items.explanation: Correct: containers share the host kernel while VMs run a full OS each.

items.stem: Which TWO practices support safe multi-workload virtualisation? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Setting resource limits so one VM cannot starve others
options.rationale: Correct: limits prevent a noisy workload from degrading the rest.
Correct: the hypervisor is a critical boundary to secure.

options.text: Using snapshots as the only long-term backup
options.rationale: Snapshots are not a substitute for proper backups.

options.text: Running every workload with no isolation
options.rationale: Removing isolation defeats a key benefit of virtualisation.

items.explanation: Correct: resource limits and a hardened hypervisor both support safe multi-workload use.

items.stem: Why are VM snapshots a poor substitute for backups over the long term?

options.text: Snapshots grow, can harm performance and depend on the same storage and host
options.rationale: Correct: snapshots are short-term and not independent copies.

options.text: Snapshots are encrypted and cannot be restored
options.rationale: Snapshots can be restored; the issue is they are not true backups.
They differ in independence and durability.
Snapshots typically stay on the same storage, not off-site.

items.explanation: Correct: snapshots are short-term, dependent on the same host/storage, and not real backups.
